manifest_rows.title: Gaussian anchored bounded sums have uniform cumulant and Fourier bounds
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $0<\gamma\le1$. Let $1\le d\le4$, $s>0$, $B>0$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_m,Z$ be independent centered random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, where $m\ge0$, $|X_j|\le B$ almost surely, and $Z\sim N_d(0,G)$. Suppose $S=Z+\sum_jX_j$ has covariance $sI_d$ and $G\ge\gamma sI_d$ in quadratic form order. There is an absolute constant $C_0\ge1$ such that, with $\tau=C_0B$, the logarithmic moment generating function
$$K(z)=\log\mathbb E e^{z\cdot S},\qquad K(0)=0,$$
has a single analytic branch on the complex Euclidean ball $\tau|z|<1$, and
$$|\partial_u\partial_v^2K(z)|\le\tau s|u||v|^2\qquad(u,v\in\mathbb R^d,\ \tau|z|<1).$$
Here $z\cdot S$ uses the complex bilinear dot product and $|z|^2=\sum_i|z_i|^2$. Every real exponential tilt $\mathbb P_h(d\omega)=e^{h\cdot S-K(h)}\mathbb P(d\omega)$ is defined, and its characteristic function satisfies
$$|\varphi_h(t)|:=|\mathbb E_h e^{it\cdot S}|\le e^{-\gamma s|t|^2/2}\qquad(t,h\in\mathbb R^d),$$
where $K(h)=\log\mathbb E e^{h\cdot S}$ for real $h$, also outside the analytic ball. Put $\kappa=\tau/\sqrt s$. For every fixed $a>0$ and integer $N\ge1$ there is a finite $C_{a,N,\gamma}$, uniform in $1\le d\le4$, such that, if $0<\kappa\le1$,
$$(2\pi)^{-d}\int_{|t|\ge a/\tau}|\varphi_h(t)|\,dt\le C_{a,N,\gamma}\kappa^Ns^{-d/2},$$
$$(2\pi)^{-d}\int_{|t|\ge a/\tau}|t\cdot v||\varphi_h(t)|\,dt\le C_{a,N,\gamma}\kappa^N|v|s^{-(d+1)/2}.$$
All assertions hold with the same $C_0$, $B$, $s$, and $\gamma$ for $AS$, where $A$ is any real $k\times d$ matrix with $1\le k\le d$ and $AA^T=I_k$. This includes every coordinate prefix, every orthogonal change of coordinates, and their compositions. In particular it covers the normalized joint sum and difference of two independent children by applying the assertion in their joint dimension, provided that dimension is at most four and the joint input satisfies the stated covariance assumptions.

references.title: A. Yu. Zaitsev, Estimates of quantiles of smooth conditional distributions and the multidimensional invariance principle, Siberian Mathematical Journal 37 (1996), §§1–2; Gaussian convolution specialization proved here

manifest_rows.title: Moderate deviation density bounds for Gaussian anchored sums
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[lem-gaussian-anchored-sums-have-cumulant-and-fourier-bounds]], with $1\le d\le4$, fixed $\gamma>0$, $\tau=C_0B$, $\kappa=\tau/\sqrt s$, and logarithmic moment generating function $K$. Let $p_h$ denote the density of $S$ under the real exponential tilt with parameter $h$. Every such density exists, is continuously differentiable and strictly positive, and
$$\sup_y p_h(y)\le(2\pi\gamma s)^{-d/2}\qquad(h\in\mathbb R^d).$$
There are constants $c_\gamma>0$, $C_\gamma<\infty$, independent of $d,s,B,m$ and the summand laws, with the following property. If $\kappa\le c_\gamma$ and $\tau|h|\le1/8$, put $\mu_h=\mathbb E_hS$ and $D_h=\operatorname{cov}_h(S)$. Then
$$\tfrac78sI_d\le D_h\le\tfrac98sI_d.$$
For $x\in\mathbb R^d$ put $r=|D_h^{-1/2}x|$ and let $q_{D_h}(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}(\det D_h)^{-1/2}e^{-r^2/2}$. Whenever $\kappa r\le c_\gamma$,
$$\left|\log\frac{p_h(\mu_h+x)}{q_{D_h}(x)}\right|\le C_\gamma\kappa(1+r^3).$$
For $r\ge7$ in the same region,
$$\left.\frac{d}{dt}\log p_h(\mu_h+x+tx)\right|_{t=0}\le-\tfrac12r^2.$$
These assertions apply separately to every row isometry image in the supplier, including every required coordinate prefix and normalized joint child sum and difference. Their tilt parameter and covariance are taken in that image's own coordinates.

manifest_rows.title: Conditional quantile couplings for Gaussian anchored sums
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[lem-gaussian-anchored-sums-have-cumulant-and-fourier-bounds]]: $S=Z+\sum_{i=1}^mX_i\in\mathbb R^d$, $1\le d\le4$, the centered summands are independent, $|X_i|\le B$, $Z$ is Gaussian with covariance $G\ge\gamma sI_d$, and $\operatorname{cov}(S)=sI_d$, where $s,B>0$ and $0<\gamma\le1$. Put $\tau=C_0B$, with $C_0$ from that supplier, and let $\Phi_s$ be the CDF of $N(0,s)$. There are constants $c_\gamma>0$ and $C_\gamma<\infty$, independent of the summand laws, $m,d,s,B$, with the following properties.

For $1\le j\le d$, let $H_j(x',y)$ be the conditional CDF of $S_j$ given $S_{<j}=x'\in\mathbb R^{j-1}$ obtained by dividing the joint prefix density by its marginal density. These densities are strictly positive, so this defines a probability kernel at every $x'$, including prefixes of probability zero. Its quantile transport
$$T_j(x',z)=H_j(x',\cdot)^{-1}(\Phi_s(z))$$
is jointly Borel measurable and takes a fresh $N(0,s)$ variable to that conditional law. If $s\ge C_\gamma\tau^2$, then, with $y=T_j(x',z)$,
$$|y-z|\le C_\gamma\tau\left(1+\frac{|x'|^2+y^2}{s}\right)\quad\hbox{when }|x'|+|y|\le c_\gamma s/\tau,$$
and also
$$|T_j(x',z)-z|\le C_\gamma\tau\left(1+\frac{|x'|^2+z^2}{s}\right)\quad\hbox{when }|x'|+|z|\le c_\gamma s/\tau.$$
For $j=1$, the prefix is empty and its norm is zero. The resulting successive coordinate transport $R$ sends $N_d(0,sI_d)$ to the law of $S$ and satisfies
$$|R(g)-g|\le C_\gamma\tau\left(1+\frac{|R(g)|^2}{s}\right)\quad\hbox{when }|R(g)|\le c_\gamma s/\tau.$$

If $d=2a$ with $a\le2$, write $S=(P,D)$ with $P,D\in\mathbb R^a$. The last $a$ successive conditional transports give a jointly measurable $T_p$ taking a fresh $E\sim N_a(0,sI_a)$ to the conditional law of $D$ given $P=p$, and
$$|T_p(e)-e|\le C_\gamma\tau\left(1+\frac{|p|^2+|T_p(e)|^2}{s}\right)$$
when $s\ge C_\gamma\tau^2$ and $|p|,|T_p(e)|\le c_\gamma s/\tau$. The Gaussian reference bridge $E$ is independent of its Gaussian parent.

There is also the following scalar unequal-variance form. Let $L,R$ be independent centered scalar sums of independent variables bounded by $B$ and independent Gaussian terms, with variances $V_L,V_R\in[s/2,s]$, and with Gaussian component variances at least $\gamma V_L,\gamma V_R$, respectively. Put
$$W=V_L+V_R,\qquad w=V_L/W,\qquad v=V_LV_R/W,\qquad P=L+R,\qquad D=L-wP.$$
Then $W\in[s,2s]$, $w\in[1/3,2/3]$, $v\in[s/4,s/2]$. There is a jointly measurable transport taking a fresh $N(0,v)$ variable to $D$ conditional on $P=p$ with
$$|T_p(e)-e|\le C_\gamma\tau\left(1+\frac{p^2+T_p(e)^2}{s}\right)$$
when $s\ge C_\gamma\tau^2$ and $|p|,|T_p(e)|\le c_\gamma s/\tau$. The corresponding root transport from $N(0,W)$ to $P$ obeys the analogous bound with $|P|^2/s$. The reconstructed children are $L=wP+D$ and $R=(1-w)P-D$.

All these maps are jointly measurable in an additional measurable parameter whenever, on each fixed finite row length, the bounded input laws are probability kernels, their Gaussian covariance and $s$ are measurable functions, and the displayed hypotheses hold parameterwise. This includes countable arrays with different row lengths. No claim here asserts the conditional estimates for raw bounded laws without a positive Gaussian component.

manifest_rows.title: Bounded independent vector rows admit a logarithmic cubed Gaussian coupling
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. For every $A>0$ there is a finite constant $C_A$, independent of all row laws and lengths, such that the following holds. Let $1\le d\le2$, $N\ge1$, $B\ge1$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$ with
$$EX_i=0,\qquad \operatorname{cov}(X_i)=I_d,\qquad |X_i|\le B\quad\hbox{almost surely}.$$
Their distributions need not be identical. There is a coupling with independent $G_1,\ldots,G_N\sim N_d(0,I_d)$ such that
$$\Pr\!\left(\max_{1\le k\le N}\left|\sum_{i=1}^k(X_i-G_i)\right|>C_AB\log^3(eN)\right)\le N^{-A}.$$
The coupling can be realized on an extension preserving an already realized raw row as its original marginal. Independence between the raw and Gaussian rows is not asserted.

manifest_rows.title: Finite-moment iid vectors admit a strong Gaussian approximation
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be iid centered vectors in $\mathbb R^2$ with $E\|X_1\|^q<\infty$ for some $q>2$. For any fixed real numbers $2<p<a<q$, on an extension preserving the original process there are independent Gaussian vectors $G_i\sim N_2(0,\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma=EX_1X_1^T$, such that almost surely
$$\max_{1\le k\le n}\left\|\sum_{i=1}^k(X_i-G_i)\right\|=O\bigl(n^{1/a}[\log(en)]^3\bigr)=o(n^{1/p}).$$
The extension can also carry a standard two-dimensional Brownian motion $B$ with $\sum_{i=1}^kG_i=\Sigma^{1/2}B(k)$ for every integer $k\ge0$. Thus, in particular, the partial-sum Brownian approximation error is $O(n^{1/p}\log n)$ almost surely. Singular covariance, including $\Sigma=0$, is permitted. Neither $B$ nor $(G_i)$ is required to be independent of $(X_i)$.
